title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Three features that were simply broken
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.31 repairs three things that were plainly broken: Organize Imports could turn the rest of a file into a comment, test coverage never appeared at all, and a `"""` written inside a comment killed the semantic colours from that line to the end of the file. Postfix completion on a safe call also stops producing Kotlin that does not compile.

highlights.title: Organize Imports keeps your file
highlights.description: A `/* … */` comment inside the import block is copied verbatim. Losing its closing line used to comment out the rest of the file.

highlights.title: Coverage finally shows up
highlights.description: The class name was read from the wrong attribute of the report, so every entry was dropped. Sources are now searched under the tested module, the KMP source sets and Java files.

highlights.title: Colours survive a quoted example
highlights.description: A `"""` written inside a comment no longer opens a raw string that never closes, which killed semantic colours and KDoc folding to the end of the file.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Organize Imports copies a `/* … */` inside the import block verbatim, and stops sorting a commented out import as a real one.
Coverage reads the class name from `name`, not `sourcefilename`, and resolves sources under the module, the KMP source sets and `.java` files.
Postfix completion on `viewModel?.` inserts code that compiles, and `let` keeps its `?.let` form.
A `"""` inside a `//` or `/* */` comment no longer disables semantic colours, occurrence highlighting and KDoc folding for the rest of the file.
The release notes panel renders the quoted file names and flags as code instead of printing backticks.
